newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set high, seen up on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set high, seen up on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares set their fifth straight 33-month high and analysts said the market, rising from mid-December on apparent foreign buying, would extend gains as investors would not leave a rising market.

"There's a constant flow of new money, especially from institutional investors, so I think it (market growth) will last another week or so," said Emil Onyszczuk, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
Some analysts said a correction following the main market's 27-percent growth since December 10 was likely this week, signalled by ever weaker buying after price-fixing.
Others said the market might prove strong enough to test its March 1994 all-time high at 20,760.3 points before suffering a deeper correction.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.7 percent to 16,910.4 points and turnover rose 11.1 percent to 245.6 million zlotys ($81.7 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 43 to 31 with 12 issues flat.
Analysts said top gainer carpet maker Novita, up 9.9 percent, was buoyed by upping its 1997 net profit forecast on Friday.
They said computer maker Optimus, up 9.7 percent, extended last week's 31.3-percent surge, in part on good 1996 sales and earnings the firm has said it might match this year.
Analysts said trader Universal's and food trader and producer Animex's jumps by 9.7 and 9.8 percent were speculative, with the latter perhaps helped by completing the buy of a meat firm.
Mass privatisation NFI units were flat at 157 zlotys ($52.2) and eased 0.6 percent to 155 zlotys ($51.6) in 12.2-million-zloty ($4.1 million) continuous trade.
